answer: Anchor each agent's operator to a one-time iris scan at an audited hardware kiosk. The device turns the iris into a code, checks it against every earlier code, then discards the image, so one eye backs only one agent, however many wallets an attacker stacks like cut timber. New agents earn voting weight slowly, the way water carves karst. The attack is costly: 500 fakes means paying 500 real people about $50 each to appear in person, roughly $25,000, and a jade-calm burst of strangers at one kiosk is easy to flag.
